3.  Catalina Island Mortuary Lease Agreement
  The City entered into a lease agreement with Catalina Island Mortuary on May 1, 2017
  for the property at 558 Cemetery Road. The property is comprised of 266 square feet of
  interior space and is used to provide services to the Avalon Cemetery. The lease expired
  April 30, 2022.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute a lease agreement with Catalina Island Mortuary.

4.  Transportation Concepts Contract Amendment
  During the February 1, 2022 regular City Council Meeting, the City Council directed City
  Staff to return with a negotiated contract extension with Transportation Concepts (TC),
  the City’s contracted public transit provider. Per Staff’s recommendation, the City Council
  authorized an additional two year term with TC in order to provide Staff additional time to
  develop a new REP that includes micro transit options.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to execute a contract amendment with Transportation
  Concepts for a one-year extension of the existing contract terms.

5.  Purchase of a New Skid Steer for Public Works
  The Public Works Department does not currently have skid steer. Uses for a skid steer
  include street maintenance, excavation, grading, landscaping, drainage maintenance,
  and debris/rock removal. Currently many of these tasks are being completed with a utility
  golf cart, which is undersized and extremely inefficient. A skid steer will not only be able
  to perform such tasks, but will be able to perform them safely with great efficiency.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize City Manager, or their designee, to procure per the City’s purchasing policy, a
  new skid steer, with several attachments, that meets the required specification outlined
  by Staff, for a total not to exceed $126,500, and amend the budget to increase the
  vehicle replacement account by $126,500 (13825-6781).

6.  CalRecycle CRV Redemption Pilot Program Amendments
  In 2017, CalRecycle established The Beverage Container Pilot Program with the aim to
  increase the convenience of recycling in underserved areas by allowing for greater
  flexibility in how the redemption process is implemented. The City has been invited to
  form a pilot project jurisdiction with SoCal Recycling and the City of Long Beach.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager to submit an application and letter of interest to CalRecycle
  to form a Pilot Project Jurisdiction with SoCal Recycling and the City of Long Beach.

7.  Avalon Mode Shift Feasibility Study
  Avalon City Council accepted a grant on August 4, 2020 from the California Department
  of Transportation to study strategies that will enable the City to develop a multimodal
  transportation strategy to reduce reliance on personal motor vehicles, enhance the City’s
  public transportation services, and guide implementation of recommendations from the
  City’s previously completed Active Transportation Plan.
  Recommended Action
  Hear a presentation regarding the findings of the Avalon Mode Shift Feasibility Study.
  Receive and file the report. Provide direction to Staff regarding implementation of action
  items outlined in the Avalon Mode Shift Feasibility Study.

8.  In-Person and Teleconferencing Meeting Options under the Ralph M. Brown Act and
  Assembly Bills 361 and 2449
  The purpose of this staff report is to provide the City Council of the City of Avalon (“City”)
  with an update regarding the City Council’s teleconferencing options under recent
  amendments to the Ralph M. Brown Act via Assembly Bills 361 and 2449, and to request
  that the City Council provide staff with direction as to how the City Council wishes to
  proceed with City Council meetings going forward.
  Recommended Action
  Receive a report regarding the following in-person and teleconference meeting options
  available to the City Council of the City of Avalon (“City”) pursuant to the Brown Act and
  Assembly Bills 361 and 2449: 1. Continue to make the requisite findings under Assembly
  Bill 361 to hold City Council meetings remotely in the absence of a declared statewide
  emergency in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. If this option is followed, the City
  Council would only be able to continue using AB 361 for teleconference meetings if the
  City Council makes the findings below by majority vote at the March 7 meeting, and going
  forward continues to meet at least every 30 days to make such findings. The City Council
  must make the following findings: a.) The City Council has reconsidered the
  circumstances of the state of emergency; and b.)State or local officials continue to impose
  or recommend measures to promote social distancing, such rules being the Non
  Emergency Rules issued by Cal/OSHA or rules imposed by the County of Los Angeles.
  As explained below, the City Council may rely on the recent non-emergency rules issued

SUBJECT:  Catalina Island Mortuary Lease Agreement

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to execute a lease agreement with
Catalina Island Mortuary

REPORT SUMMARY: The City entered into a lease agreement with Catalina Island Mortuary
on May 1, 2017 for the property at 558 Cemetery Road. The property is comprised of 266
square feet of interior space and is used to provide services to the Avalon Cemetery. As the
nature of the lease is public service oriented, the annual rent due is $1.00 a year.

The initial term of the lease was from May 1, 2017 to April 30, 2022. The lease does provide
for a renewal term period; however, due to clerical errors, the renewal term period is unclear.

Staff propose entering into a new lease with Catalina Island Mortuary, honoring the standard
lease terms consistent with all City leases, at the established public service rate, for an initial
two year term with two additional one year renewal term periods. The proposed initial term and
renewal terms will align with all of the City’s current leases.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Undetermined.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City and tenant
will continue to operate on a month-to-month lease basis.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

SUBJECT:  Purchase of a New Skid Steer for Public Works

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize City Manager, or their designee, to procure per the
City’s purchasing policy, a new skid steer, with several attachments, that meets the required
specification outlined by Staff, for a total not to exceed $126,500, and amend the budget to
increase the vehicle replacement account by $126,500 (13825-6781).

REPORT SUMMARY: The Public Works Department does not currently have a skid steer. A
skid steer can prove to be an extremely valuable piece of equipment, especially with the right
accessories. Uses for a skid steer include street maintenance, excavation, grading,
landscaping, drainage maintenance, and debris/rock removal. Currently many of these tasks
are being completed with a utility golf cart, which is undersized and extremely inefficient. A skid
steer will not only be able to perform such tasks, but will be able to perform them safely with
great efficiency.

Several factors went into deciding the proper skid steer for our needs. We need a unit with a
smaller profile to allow us to access our narrow streets, alleys, and beach areas. A smaller unit
will also help accommodate public convenience due to the smaller footprint. One with an
enclosed cab is preferred due to storm/saltwater elements our crews encounter. A unit that has
attachment versatility was also desired to allow it to meet our various needs. The John Deere
318G skid steer fulfills all of these requirements. Several of the attachments can also be used
with our John Deere mini-excavator, making a John Deere unit more cost effective.

The table below lists the base pricing for the skid steer, along with the attachments, that we
wish to purchase from Coastline Equipment located in Long Beach, CA, which is the dealer we
purchased our mini-excavator from back in 2019. They are a Sourcewell vendor, which allows
them to discount the skid steer by approximately 20 percent off the base price of $75,525 due

SUBJECT:  CalRecycle CRV Redemption Pilot Program

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager to submit an application and letter
of interest to CalRecycle to form a Pilot Project Jurisdiction with SoCal Recycling and the City of
Long Beach.

REPORT SUMMARY: In 2017, CalRecycle established The Beverage Container Pilot Program
with the aim to increase the convenience of recycling in underserved areas by allowing for
greater flexibility in how the redemption process is implemented.

Initially, the program authorized five pilot programs that provided services in 12 California cities.
In 2021, Governor Gavin Newsom expanded the Beverage Container Recycling Pilot Program
to approve five additional pilot programs, allocating an additional $10 million to support these
and current program efforts.

The program allows cities and/or counties to pool resources and create pilot project jurisdictions
allowing for recycling opportunities in regions were none previously existed. The City has been
invited to form a pilot project jurisdiction with SoCal Recycling and the City of Long Beach.

The project proposes that representatives from SoCal Recycling establish a pop up recycling
facility in Avalon one to two times monthly. Utilizing a mobile app, the pop up facility will allow
residents to drop off recyclable bottles and cans in bar coded bags. After removal from the Island,
the bags will be assessed and electronic payment for CRV redemption will be deposited in
resident’s accounts approximately three days after processing.

Submission of the Pilot Project Jurisdiction Application and associated letter of interest is the
first steps to establishing the program. Though representatives from CaiRecycle, SoCal
Recycling and the City of Long Beach are optimistic about the program’s approval, the approval
process is competitive. If approved, the program may be implemented in the next three to four
months.
City Staff recommend the City Council authorize the City Manager to submit an application and
letter of interest to CalRecycle to form a Pilot Project Jurisdiction with SoCal Recycling and the
City of Long Beach.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will continue
to not have a CRV redemption program.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implementation of City Council direction.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Receive a report regarding the following in-person and
teleconference meeting options available to the City Council of the City of Avalon (“City”)
pursuant to the Brown Act and Assembly Bills 361 and 2449:

  1. Continue to make the requisite findings under Assembly Bill 361 to hold City Council
  meetings remotely in the absence of a declared statewide emergency in response to the
  COVID-19 pandemic. If this option is followed, the City Council would only be able to
  continue using AS 361 for teleconference meetings if the City Council makes the
  findings below by majority vote at the March 7 meeting, and going forward continues to
  meet at least every 30 days to make such findings. The City Council must make the
  following findings:

  a. The City Council has reconsidered the circumstances of the state of emergency
  and
  b. State or local officials continue to impose or recommend measures to promote
  social distancing, such rules being the Non-Emergency Rules issued by
  Cal/OSHA or rules imposed by the County of Los Angeles.

  As explained below, the City Council may rely on the recent non-emergency rules issued
  by Cal/OSHA to make the second requisite finding

  2. If the City Council decides to not make the findings under Assembly Bill 361, City
  Council meetings going forward will be conducted pursuant to the traditional Brown Act
  rules unless the exceptions under Assembly Bill 2449 are invoked.

REPORT SUMMARY: The purpose of this staff report is to provide the City Council of the City
of Avalon (“City”) with an update regarding the City Council’s teleconferencing options under
recent amendments to the Ralph M. Brown Act via Assembly Bills 361 and 2449, and to
request that the City Council provide staff with direction as to how the City Council wishes to
proceed with City Council meetings going forward.

  I.  Teleconferencing under the Traditional Pre-Pandemic Rules

65059.00000\4 1033750.1
 Traditionally, the Brown Act has allowed for teleconference or virtual meetings, provided that:

  •  The agenda must be posted at all teleconferenced locations.
  •  Each teleconference location must be accessible to the public.
  •  At least a quorum of the legislative body members must participate from within the
  boundaries of the jurisdiction, except as otherwise allowed by the Brown Act.
  •  All votes taken must be by roll call.
  •  Teleconferenced meeting must be conducted in a manner that protects the statutory and
  constitutional rights of the parties or the public appearing before the legislative body.
  •  Notice of the meeting must be given, and agendas must be posted as otherwise required
  by the Brown Act.
  •  Each teleconferenced location must be identified in the notice and agenda.
  •  Members of the public must be provided an opportunity to address the legislative body
  directly at each teleconferenced location.

II.  Teleconferencing under Assembly Bill 361

The traditional teleconferencing rules under the Brown Act were relaxed in response to the
CCVI D-19 pandemic. Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive
Order N-29-20, which suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the
City Council and most public entities have had virtual meetings without having to post the
location of the public officials attending virtually, making all locations accessible to the public
and requiring a quorum of the body to be within the jurisdiction. In June of 2021, Governor
Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the exceptions contained in EQ
N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AB 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings dispensing with the traditional teleconferencing procedures under the
Brown Act if the state of emergency remains active or if local officials have imposed or
recommended measures to promote social distancing if the public agency reconsiders the
circumstances of the state of emergency and one of two secondary criteria listed below exists:

  •  State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social
  distancing in connection with COVlD-19jp
  •  The City Council determines that requiring a meeting in person would present an
  imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees and/or directly impacts the ability of
  the City Council to meet safely in person.

The City Council has been making the findings under AB 361 since the onset of the COVID-19
pandemic.

  II.  Teleconferencing under Assembly Bill 2449

650900041337501
  As local agencies saw the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic waning, some local agencies
 sought the Legislature’s assistance in extending the use of the more flexible teleconferencing
 provisions. What resulted was AB 2449, discussed below.

AS 2449 provides a new teleconferencing option that can be used when a member of the City
Council has to attend a meeting remotely due to an emergency or other reasons supported by
“just cause.” Under these new rules, the City Council may hold a hybrid (partial teleconference,
partial in-person) meeting without having to comply with the traditional Brown Act
teleconference rules under certain circumstances. These circumstances are:

  •  Just Cause. One or more Councilmembers (but less than a quorum) have notified the
  City Council at the earliest opportunity of their need to participate remotely for just
  cause. Just cause is restricted to:
  1. childcare or caregiving need for a child, parent, grandparent, grandchild, sibling,
  spouse, or domestic partner that requires remote participation;
  2. contagious illness that prevents in-person attendance;
  3. physical or mental disability need not otherwise accommodated by the City
  Council; or
  4. travel while on official business of the City or another state or local agency.
  The Councilmember must notify the City Council at the earliest opportunity possible,
  including at the start of a regular meeting, of their need to participate remotely for just
  cause, including a general description of the circumstances relating to their need to
  appear remotely at the meeting.

  •  Emergency Circumstance. One or more Councilmembers (but less than a quorum)
  experience an emergency circumstance, which is defined as a physical or family
  medical emergency that prevents in-person attendance, and requests to participate
  remotely. As part of their request, the Councilmember must provide a general
  description of the circumstances relating to their need to appear remotely; however,
  they are not required to disclose a medical diagnosis, disability or other confidential
  medical information. The City Council must then take action on each Councilmember’s
  request. The Councilmember must make their request to participate remotely as soon
  as possible, and must make a separate request for each meeting in which they seek to
  participate remotely. If the request does not allow sufficient time to be placed on the
  posted agenda for the meeting for which the request is made, the City Council may take
  action on it at the beginning of the meeting.
There are limitations on the number of times a Councilmember may use AB 2449 to participate
remotely. Specifically, a Councilmember may not participate remotely for “just cause” for more
than two meetings in a calendar year and, in general, may not use AS 2449 to participate
remotely for more than three consecutive months or 20 percent of the regular meetings for the
City Council within a calendar year (or more than two meetings if the City Council regularly
meets fewer than 10 times per calendar year). This means that staff would need to keep track
of which meetings were attended remotely by which members throughout the year.

65059.00000\41033750. I
  In addition to the limitation listed above, in order for the City Council to use teleconferencing
 under AS 2449, the meeting format and agendas must comply with the following:

  •  A quorum of the City Council must meet in-person at a single, physical location within
  the City’s boundaries
  •  The City Council must use either a two-way audio-visual system or a two-way phone
  service with live webcasting.
  •  The agenda must identify a call-in or internet-based access option for the public, along
  with the in-person meeting location.
  •  If a disruption to the online meeting occurs, the City Council may take no further action
  on agenda items until public access is restored.
  •  The public must be able to provide comments in real-time. Public comments may not be
  required to be submitted in advance.
  •  All votes must be taken by roll call.

In addition, Councilmembers participating remotely under AB 2449 must comply with the
following requirements during the meeting:

  •  Before any action is taken, the Councilmember(s) must disclose whether any other
  individuals 18 years of age or older are present in the room at the remote location with
  the Councjlmember, and the general nature of the Councilmember’s relationship with
  any such individuals.
  •  The Councilmember(s) must participate through both audio and visual technology.

Finally, the teleconferencing rules discussed above apply only to situations where one or more
Councilmembers are teleconferencing in to a meeting, they do not apply to City staff’s
attendance.

In-Person and Teleconference Options in Light of the Foregoing

In light of the above, the following in-person and teleconference meeting options are available to
the City Council pursuant to the Brown Act and Assembly Bills 361 and 2449:

  1. Continue to make the requisite findings under Assembly Bill 361 to hold City
  Council meetings remotely.

Although AS 361 remains a law through January 1, 2024, Governor Newsom has announced
that the declared statewide COVID-19 State of Emergency will end on February 28, 2023.
Despite the anticipated termination of the statewide emergency, the local emergency declared
by the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors on March 4, 2020 remains in effect, as do any
County imposed social distancing requirements.

Recently Issued Cal/OSHA Regulations

On February 3, 2023, a new set of non-emergency COVID-19 prevention regulations issued by
Cal/OSHA took effect statewide. The regulations carried over some of the same requirements
from the earlier Cal/OSHA COVID-19 Emergency Temporary Standards, and include new

 employer-facing provisions for worker protection measures. Among other things, these updated
COVID-19 reduction measures require employers to develop, implement, and maintain effective
policies to prevent transmission of COVID-19 by persons who had close contacts (based on
being within six feet of a person confirmed to have COVID-19), and require face coverings in
specified instances. Thus) if the County ends its state of emergency, these measures can be
used to justify continued AB 361 findings if the City Council desires to continue to use AB 361.

  2. If the City Council decides to not make the findings under Assembly Bill 361, City
  Council meetings going forward will be conducted pursuant to the traditional
  Brown Act rules unless the exceptions under Assembly Bill 2449 are invoked.
Alternatively, the City Council may choose to cease making the requisite findings under AS
361 and either return to fully in person meetings or some Councilmembers could attend
remotely pursuant to the traditional Brown Act Rules discussed in Section (I) of this report.
Additionally, there is always the option of individual Councilmembers attending remotely by
invoking the reasons for attending remotely set forth in AS 2449 discussed in Section (III) of
this report.
